title: The completed triangular flow is unique and propagates the constraints

completed_constraints.uniqueness: The K1392 one-tier difference inequality with zero initial difference gives uniqueness in C X_R intersect C^1 X_(R-1)
completed_constraints.continuous_dependence: Gronwall gives Z_R(t)<=Z_R(0) exp(C_R integral_0^t (1+Y_(R+1)+Ytilde_(R+1))^2 ds) on every common local interval
completed_constraints.current_limit: The cutoff currents converge in C H^(R-1), so K1374's distributional continuity equation partial_mu j^mu=0 passes to the completed solution
completed_constraints.lorenz_constraint: The Lorenz defect obeys the homogeneous scalar wave equation and remains zero from compatible initial data
completed_constraints.gauss_constraint: The Gauss defect is constant in time in H^(R-2) and remains zero from compatible initial data
completed_constraints.brst_scope: The Abelian BRST formulas remain nilpotent on the dense smooth common core and are closable between adjacent triangular graph tiers; no closed nonlinear KT range follows
completed_constraints.flow_map: The local solution map is single-valued and continuous from bounded X_(R+1) sets into C X_R intersect C^1 X_(R-1)
completed_constraints.boundary: Analytic constraint propagation and a continuous gauge-fixed flow are not a proper BV-BFV quotient, a positive physical cohomology theorem or source identification
